item.title: 'For their whole life, the Arahants have abandoned non-celibacy, live the celibate life, live aloof, abstain from the vulgar practice of sexual intercourse. Today, this…
item.description:
'For their whole life, the Arahants have abandoned non-celibacy, live the celibate life, live aloof, abstain from the vulgar practice of sexual intercourse. Today, this night and this day, I also abandon non-celibacy, live the celibate life, live aloof, abstain from the vulgar practice of sexual intercourse. By this factor, following the example of the Arahants, I will observe the uposatha day.'

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 8.41

item.title: Questioner: He with open eyes has clearly declared The Dhamma that can be known, overcoming all dangers. Please, O good one, explain the path, Or…
item.description:
Questioner:
He with open eyes has clearly declared
The Dhamma that can be known, overcoming all dangers.
Please, O good one, explain the path,
Or about specific liberation, or about jhāna.

The Blessed One:
Do not be greedy for forms!
Block your ears to the noise of the village!
Do not be attached to tastes!
Let nothing in the world be considered 'mine'!

When contacted by contacts, let a bhikkhu not lament over anything.
Let him not long for any kind of existence,
And let him not tremble in the face of terrors.

Having obtained food and drink, solid food and clothing,
Let him not hoard them; if he does not obtain them, let him not be anxious.

Let him practice jhāna, not wandering about,
Not delighting in restlessness, not falling into heedlessness.
Let him dwell in silent lodgings, in seats and beds.

Let him sleep little, be wakeful, ardent,
Abandon laziness, deceit, laughter, play,
Sexual intercourse, and all adornments.

Let him not tremble when blamed,
Nor be elated when praised.
Let him abandon greed, stinginess, anger, and divisive speech.

Let him not engage in buying and selling,
Nor criticize anyone anywhere.
Let him not be angry in the village,
Nor, for the sake of gain, talk with people.

Let a bhikkhu not speak boastfully,
Nor speak with an ulterior motive.
Let him not train in insolence,
Nor utter provocative words.

Let him not be led into false speech,
Nor intentionally do deceitful things.
Let him not despise others for their life,
Their wisdom, or their virtue.

Having heard harsh words from ascetics or ordinary people,
Let him not respond with harsh words;
The peaceful, gentle one does not retaliate.

Knowing this Dhamma, a bhikkhu should train
Mindfully, always comprehending.
Knowing the state of peace, he is called 'calmed'.
Do not be heedless in Gotama's teaching.

He who is victorious is not defeated;
He sees the Dhamma for himself, not by hearsay.
Therefore, always train heedfully
With respect for the Blessed One's teaching.

From: Sutta Nipāta 4.14

item.title: - Where, Venerable Sir, should a gift be given?" - "Great King, wherever the mind finds confidence." - "Venerable Sir, where does a gift yield…
item.description:
- Where, Venerable Sir, should a gift be given?" - "Great King, wherever the mind finds confidence." - "Venerable Sir, where does a gift yield great fruit?" - "Great King, the question 'Where should a gift be given?' is one thing, and the question 'Where does a gift yield great fruit?' is another. Great King, giving to a virtuous one yields great fruit, not so to an immoral one. Regarding this, Great King, I will ask you a question; answer as you like. What do you think, Great King? Here, Great King, you are engaged in battle, and a fierce battle is raging. Then a young noble warrior comes, unlearned, untrained, unpracticed, inexperienced, timid, fearful, terrified. Would you accept him, would you employ him? Would such a one be of any use to you?" - "No, Venerable Sir, I would not accept him, nor would such a one be of any use to me." - "What do you think, Great King? Here, you are engaged in battle, and a fierce battle is raging. Then a young noble warrior comes, learned, trained, practiced, experienced, not timid, not fearful, not terrified. Would you accept him, would you employ him? Would such a one be of any use to you?" - "Yes, Venerable Sir, I would accept him, and such a one would be of use to me." - "So too, Great King, whether one has gone forth from any family, from home to homelessness, if he has abandoned five factors and possesses five factors, giving to such a person yields great fruit. What five factors are abandoned? Sensual desire is abandoned, ill-will is abandoned, sloth and torpor are abandoned, restlessness and remorse are abandoned, doubt is abandoned. These five factors are abandoned. What five factors are possessed? The aggregate of noble virtue is possessed, the aggregate of noble concentration is possessed, the aggregate of noble wisdom is possessed, the aggregate of noble liberation is possessed, the aggregate of noble knowledge and vision of liberation is possessed. These five factors are possessed. Giving to such a person, who has abandoned five factors and possesses five factors, yields great fruit.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 3.24

item.title: Elder Sumaṅgala: Well released! Well released indeed! Truly I am well released from three crooked things: From sickles, from ploughs, from hoes. If there is…
item.description:
Elder Sumaṅgala:

Well released! Well released indeed!
Truly I am well released from three crooked things:
From sickles, from ploughs, from hoes.
If there is this, there is this — enough disgust, enough disgust!
O Sumaṅgala! Meditate, O Sumaṅgala! O Sumaṅgala, live heedfully!

From: Theragāthā 1.43

item.title: Just as, bhikkhus, in a king's frontier fortress there is a high, wide wall, with a coating of plaster on the outside, to protect those…
item.description:
Just as, bhikkhus, in a king's frontier fortress there is a high, wide wall, with a coating of plaster on the outside, to protect those inside the fortress and to keep out those outside. So too, bhikkhus, a noble disciple has wisdom, possessing wisdom that penetrates arising and passing away, with the noble penetration leading to the complete destruction of suffering. Using wisdom as the plaster coating, bhikkhus, the noble disciple abandons the unwholesome, develops the wholesome, abandons what is blameworthy, develops what is blameless, and keeps himself pure. With this seventh excellent quality he is accomplished.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 7.67

item.title: Poṭṭhapāda, what are the teachings that I have declared and explained definitively? 'This is suffering,' Poṭṭhapāda, that is a teaching I have declared definitively. 'This…
item.description:
Poṭṭhapāda, what are the teachings that I have declared and explained definitively? 'This is suffering,' Poṭṭhapāda, that is a teaching I have declared definitively. 'This is the origin of suffering,' Poṭṭhapāda, that is a teaching I have declared definitively. 'This is the cessation of suffering,' Poṭṭhapāda, that is a teaching I have declared definitively. 'This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering,' Poṭṭhapāda, that is a teaching I have declared definitively.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 9 – Poṭṭhapādasutta

item.title: Those who are excessively attached, Confused about things, Led astray by various sects, They sleep on and on, They are not awake. Now indeed it…
item.description:
Those who are excessively attached,
Confused about things,
Led astray by various sects,
They sleep on and on,
They are not awake.
Now indeed it is time
For them to awaken.
( Blessed One ):
Those who are not excessively attached,
Not confused about things,
Not led astray by various sects,
They have attained perfect enlightenment.
They fully understand perfectly,
On the uneven path,
They walk evenly.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.8

item.title: - What binds the world? By taming what is one freed? By abandoning what thing Are all bonds cut? - Desire binds the world, By…
item.description:
- What binds the world?
By taming what is one freed?
By abandoning what thing
Are all bonds cut?
- Desire binds the world,
By taming desire one is freed,
By abandoning desire
Are all bonds cut.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.69

item.title: Time passes silently, Nights and days move quickly, Youth abandons us, One by one. Those who contemplate this fear of death, Should do meritorious deeds…
item.description:
Time passes silently,
Nights and days move quickly,
Youth abandons us,
One by one.
Those who contemplate this fear of death,
Should do meritorious deeds
That bring happiness.

( Blessed One ):
Time passes silently,
Nights and days move quickly,
Youth abandons us,
One by one.
Those who contemplate this fear of death,
Should abandon worldly gains,
Attain true peace.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.27

item.title: He avoids wrong livelihood such as: consulting mirrors, consulting female mediums, consulting devas for signs of good or evil, worshipping the sun, worshipping the earth,…
item.description:
He avoids wrong livelihood such as: consulting mirrors, consulting female mediums, consulting devas for signs of good or evil, worshipping the sun, worshipping the earth, spitting fire, invoking the goddess of fortune, using spells for good luck or causing misfortune. Such is his virtue in terms of moral discipline.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 2 – Sāmaññaphalasutta
